brief: Doctrine rewrite of 2026-08-21: every line is about the weather; the picture is the evidence. Three lines per photograph (Al’s ruled keeps locked and counted). Bank rescues marked. PAIRING-TASTE + the swap test still bind.
linesLabel: three per image incl. locked keeps

images.seen: A runner stretching against a green wall on a cobbled Bo-Kaap street at dawn, painted houses running down to the city, pearly overcast sky. Saturday.
lines: The sun is up there somewhere behind three layers of Saturday-morning grey.
The Bo-Kaap does the colour this morning because the sky refuses to.
Cool, grey and windless — honestly the best running weather this city sells.

images.seen: A painter up a ladder painting a Bo-Kaap house turquoise under a flat overcast sky, coffee mug and paint tin on the windowsill. Tuesday.
lines: Flat grey light, no glare, no wind: perfect painting weather, and he knows it.
An overcast sky is a painter's softbox — not one hard shadow on that wall.
The cloud came in overnight and parked; nothing under it is in a hurry.

images.seen: A toddler in grey pyjamas at a floor-to-ceiling window, hands on the glass, looking out over a grey misty city, warm lamp inside. Sunday.
lines: The whole city is under one grey blanket and somebody just noticed.
A lid like that takes until about eleven to lift, if it lifts at all.
The sky is buffering.

images.seen: Merino sheep bunched tight on dry Karoo veld, shepherd and dog in the distance, heavy grey cloud deck with one shaft of sun breaking through. Wednesday.
lines: The sun is down to one beam and the whole veld is watching where it lands.
The sheep bunched up an hour ago, which is the Karoo's own forecast.
That grey is thinking about rain and the whole district is thinking with it.

images.seen: A vertical wall of grey cloud splitting the sky over empty Karoo grassland — clear blue on the left, heavy grey with rain veils on the right. Monday.
lines: Half the sky has an opinion and the other half is about to hear it.
The week's weather is changing hands right there, in one straight line.
Blue on the left, business on the right, and the line is moving your way.

images.seen: White sheets pegged on a T-pole washing line, hanging dead still under a heavy grey sky, green lawn and strelitzias below. Thursday.
lines: That washing is a straight bet against that sky, and the sky looks confident.
Not a breath moving those sheets, and nothing helpful coming from above either.
Grey like that can hold all day without dropping a thing — probably.

images.seen: Two long-haired dachshunds at a sliding door, looking out at a grey garden through glass still dotted with drizzle. Friday.
lines: The walk has been postponed by the committee upstairs, and the committee looks settled.
The sky is doing nothing in particular and being very thorough about it.
The sun sent an out-of-office reply.

images.seen: A road cyclist paused at the top of a mountain-pass switchback at dusk, broken grey cloud with gold-lit patches over a valley of farms. Monday.
lines: The sky saved its best ten minutes for the top of the climb.
Cloud all afternoon, and now this — the sky apologising in gold.
That gap in the cloud is worth more than the whole clear day it replaced.

images.seen: A vineyard wedding at dusk — couple posing, photographer kneeling, mother-of-the-bride in a hat looking up at a pink-grey broken sky, Cape Dutch manor behind. Saturday.
lines: One person at this wedding is checking the sky, and she has been right before.
The clouds came dressed in pink for the occasion and are behaving so far.
That sky will hold for the photographs — after that, no promises.

images.seen: A crescent moon fighting through heavy broken cloud over a dark Karoo plain, one low koppie on the horizon. Monday.
lines: The moon is down to one small window and it is using all of it.
The clouds are winning tonight, about nine rounds to one.
A sky like that keeps the heat in — the frost can stand down tonight.

images.seen: A Bengal cat curled asleep on a couch against a knitted blanket, lamp lit, heavy dark cloud over distant city lights through the window. Wednesday.
lines: Cloud right down to the rooftops, and every sensible mammal is indoors under a lamp.
Nothing is falling and nothing is shining; it is that kind of night.
A sky with no stars is the sky's way of saying go to bed.

images.seen: A white bakkie with headlights blazing on a dead-straight Karoo road at night, one bare thorn tree beside it, a completely starless overcast sky. Friday.
lines: No moon, no stars, no streetlights: tonight the headlights are the whole sky.
The sky has switched itself off for the night; the bakkie disagrees.
Overcast this thick turns the Karoo into a corridor, and he is halfway down it.

images.seen: A farmer with a torch walking towards a windpomp at night, full moon glowing through a mackerel sky of broken cloud, Karoo scrub. Tuesday.
lines: The moon has enough cloud to fight through that the torch got the job.
Cloud like fish scales means the weather is thinking about changing its mind.
That cloud is just thick enough to make the moon count for nothing on the ground.

images.seen: Two fishermen in yellow oilskins and headlamps pushing a boat on its trailer down a slipway at grey dawn, breath visible, flat pewter sea, heavy overcast on the mountains. Monday.
lines: Grey sky, flat sea, visible breath: the exact morning the fish expect them.
The cloud is sitting right on the mountains and the sea has gone pewter.
No wind on the water this morning, which is worth more than sunshine out there.

images.seen: A newspaper seller working a Joburg intersection at dawn under a pink-grey overcast winter sky, steaming enamel mug on the curb, red robots behind. Friday.
lines: That mug is steaming because Joburg mornings under cloud start at about four degrees.
The cloud kept the frost off the windscreens, which is the one favour it does.
Pink-grey sky over the robots: winter is on the morning shift too.

images.seen: A trail runner on a stone coastal path above a churning grey sea, a huge brooding cloud bank overhead with one thin light break at the horizon. Wednesday.
lines: The sky brought its full weight this morning and the sea rose to meet it.
One thin line of light at the horizon, and the whole sky leaning on it.
Running weather, honestly: cool, grey, and the sea doing the soundtrack.

images.seen: A paved walkway through a stone-walled coastal village at grey dawn, heavy cloud with one weak sun break over a rough sea. Thursday.
lines: The sun is trying its luck at the horizon and the cloud is unmoved.
The sea keeps its winter colour under a sky like this, whatever the calendar says.
A grey start on the coast usually burns off by ten. Usually.

images.seen: A woman in a navy swimsuit on a striped towel on a lawn, sunscreen in hand, squinting up at a dark grey cloud bank with blue sky still visible behind it, plumbago hedge and white gable house. Saturday.
lines: The cloud arrived about four minutes after the towel went down, which is policy.
Sunscreen out, sun gone: the sky has a sense of humour today.
The blue sky is still back there somewhere, but the grey has the floor.

images.seen: An empty school rugby field with white posts under a flat grey sky, dry koppies and a red-brick school building behind. Wednesday.
lines: Flat grey over the rugby field: perfect kicking weather, no wind to blame.
The sky has gone the colour of the staff-room ceiling and settled in.
A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.

images.seen: A chameleon halfway along a bare branch, heavy grey cloud filling the sky, garden leaves and a terracotta roof below. Friday.
lines: The one animal that can match the sky's mood is having no trouble today.
Every leaf is holding still; the whole garden is waiting to see what the sky decides.
The clouds are here but they're not doing anything.

images.seen: A man lighting wood chips with a gas lighter on a brick braai under a heavy dark grey sky, meat already on the grid, wet paving, charcoal bag and firelighters at hand. Sunday.
lines: That sky can do what it wants; the wors is already on.
The sky is threatening, the firelighters are answering: a very South African standoff.
Paving wet, clouds low, fire going anyway — this braai has been through worse.

images.seen: A blazing red-pink cloud sunset over the Table Mountain silhouette, seen from the dunes at Blouberg, one person standing in the dune grass. Sunday.
lines: Cloud is what a sunset needs, and tonight the sky brought exactly enough.
Table Mountain gets the silhouette; the clouds get the whole colour budget.
Red sky at night, shepherd's delight — tomorrow just got a good reference.

images.seen: A dog in a grey knitted jersey curled up on an outdoor cushion at dusk, heavy grey cloud over the mountains behind the patio. Tuesday.
lines: The dog is wearing a jersey, which is all the forecast anybody here needs.
Grey sky, grey jersey: the whole stoep is colour-coordinated with the weather.
The day never warmed up, and one resident has stopped waiting for it to.

images.seen: A burning orange sunset squeezed into a thin gap under a huge dark cloud bank, suburban rooftops and misty trees below, mountain silhouette on the horizon. Wednesday.
lines: The sky left a two-finger gap for the sunset and the sunset took it.
All that cloud, and the sun still found the letterbox at the bottom.
The suburb is going to bed under a lid, with one orange nightlight left on.

images.seen: Suburban rooftops bristling with old TV aerials at dusk, grey cloud with soft pink underlight, a few windows glowing warm. Thursday.
lines: The clouds took the sunset and left the suburb the pink change.
The aerials have the best view of a sky doing its quiet closing number.
A grey dusk brings the evening forward, and the windows have already agreed.

images.seen: A lone braai stand and wooden picnic table on cracked dry veld outside town, charcoal bag on the table, huge dark cloud deck with one orange band at the horizon. Friday.
lines: The charcoal is out, the sky is undecided, and neither is backing down.
That cloud has been rehearsing all afternoon and still hasn't said its line.
The horizon kept one strip of orange as proof the sun was here.

images.seen: A man in a puffer jacket and headphones reclining on a rooftop deckchair at night, the overcast sky glowing orange with the city's light. Sunday.
lines: The cloud is holding the city's glow like a lampshade tonight.
Overcast at night keeps the warmth in, and somebody is out here using it.
No stars on offer tonight, so the city is providing its own.

images.seen: Three friends wrapped in blankets around a lantern on a stone patio at night, wine and snacks on the table, pitch-dark heavy cloud over the valley. Saturday.
lines: The sky brought nothing tonight, so the lantern is carrying the whole evening.
Blankets outside in the dark: the evening is cold, the company is not.
Not one star made it through that lid, and nobody has noticed yet.

images.seen: A man in a beanie and scarf walking a small terrier along the Sea Point promenade at night, lampposts glowing, cloud pouring over Lion's Head, dark calm sea. Thursday.
lines: The cloud is coming over the mountain like it pays rent here.
That cloud will be down on the streetlights before the walk is done.
Low cloud at night keeps the cold off the promenade, and the regulars know it.

images.seen: A man in slops standing beside his mower on a half-mowed lawn, looking up at a heavy grey sky over the mountain, beer waiting on the patio table. Saturday.
lines: Half a lawn mowed, and now the negotiation with the sky begins.
The sky is deciding whether the second half of that lawn happens today.
That look is a man asking the clouds for forty-five more minutes.

images.seen: A woman jogging along the Umhlanga promenade past the whalebone pier arches, pearly overcast sky over a warm grey sea, her ponytail lifting in the breeze. Sunday.
lines: Durban grey is still twenty-four degrees, which is why the promenade never empties.
The cloud is doing sunscreen duty this morning and the runners are cashing in.
A pearl-grey sky and a warm sea breeze: the coast's version of mild.

images.seen: A man standing on his tiled roof beside new solar panels, hands on hips, giving a fully grey sky a skeptical look. Tuesday.
lines: Panels installed, sun absent: the sky owes this roof an apology.
Grey from gutter to gutter, and every kilowatt up here is on standby.
The forecast said partly sunny; the sky went with fully committed grey.

images.seen: A scruffy dog lying on a blanket on a stoep beside strelitzias, damp concrete, heavy grey sky over a lush garden. Tuesday.
lines: A grey day reads the same in any language: blanket, stoep, minimal ambition.
The concrete is still damp and the sky looks like it isn't finished.
Under a sky like this the whole garden runs at half-speed, dog included.

images.seen: A man at the end of his wet driveway, back to camera, umbrella in one hand and sunglasses in the other, under a broken grey sky with bright patches. Thursday.
lines: Umbrella in one hand, sunglasses in the other — he has met this sky before.
That sky refuses to commit, so he came prepared for both of its moods.
Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.

images.seen: An estate street split down the middle — deep blue sky and sunlit lawns on one side, a dark advancing wall of cloud on the other. Monday.
lines: Half this street is in summer and the other half is about to be somewhere else.
That cloud line is moving in with the confidence of a Monday.
The blue half of the sky is on borrowed time and the lawns know it.
